vsm1.3:74.1: Now, as to the words, one that suits his temperament (§28):
vsm1.3:74.2: there are six kinds of temperament, that is,
vsm1.3:74.3: greedy temperament, hating temperament, deluded temperament,
vsm1.3:74.4: faithful temperament, intelligent temperament, and speculative temperament.
vsm1.3:74.5:
Some would have fourteen, taking these six single ones together with the four made up of the three
double combinations and one triple combination with the greed triad
vsm1.3:74.6: and likewise with the faith triad.
vsm1.3:74.7: But if this classification is admitted,
vsm1.3:74.8: there are many more kinds of temperament possible by combining greed, etc., with faith, etc.;
vsm1.3:74.9: therefore the kinds of temperament should be understood briefly as only six.
vsm1.3:74.10: As to meaning the temperaments are one, that is to say, personal nature, idiosyncrasy.
vsm1.3:74.11: According to these there are only six types of persons, that is,
vsm1.3:74.12: one of greedy temperament, one of hating temperament, one of deluded temperament,
vsm1.3:74.13: one of faithful temperament, one of intelligent temperament, and one of speculative temperament.
vsm1.3:75.1:
Herein, one of faithful temperament is parallel to one of greedy temperament because faith
is strong when profitable kamma occurs in one of greedy temperament,
vsm1.3:75.2: owing to its special qualities being near to those of greed.
vsm1.3:75.3: For, in an unprofitable way, greed is affectionate and not over-austere, and so, in a profitable way, is faith.
vsm1.3:75.4: Greed seeks out sense desires as object, while faith seeks out the special qualities of virtue and so on.
vsm1.3:75.5: And greed does not give up what is harmful, while faith does not give up what is beneficial.
vsm1.3:76.1:
One of intelligent temperament is parallel to one of hating temperament because understanding
is strong when profitable kamma occurs in one of hating temperament,
vsm1.3:76.2: owing to its special qualities being near to those of hate.
vsm1.3:76.3: For, in an unprofitable way, hate is disaffected and does not hold to its object, and so, in a profitable way, is understanding.
vsm1.3:76.4: Hate seeks out only unreal faults, while understanding seeks out only real faults.
vsm1.3:76.5: And hate occurs in the mode of condemning living beings, while understanding occurs in the mode of condemning formations.
vsm1.3:77.1:
One of speculative temperament is parallel to one of deluded temperament because obstructive applied thoughts
arise often in one of deluded temperament who is striving to arouse unarisen profitable states,
vsm1.3:77.2: owing to their special qualities being near to those of delusion.
vsm1.3:77.3: For just as delusion is restless owing to perplexity, so are applied thoughts that are due to thinking over various aspects.
vsm1.3:77.4: And just as delusion vacillates owing to superficiality, so do applied thoughts that are due to facile conjecturing.
vsm1.3:78.1: Others say that there are three more kinds of temperament with craving, pride, and views.
vsm1.3:78.2: Herein craving is simply greed; and pride is associated with that, so neither of them exceeds greed.
vsm1.3:78.3: And since views have their source in delusion, the temperament of views falls within the deluded temperament.
vsm1.3:79.1: What is the source of these temperaments?
vsm1.3:79.2: And how is it to be known
vsm1.3:79.3: that such a person is of greedy temperament,
vsm1.3:79.4: that such a person is of one of those beginning with hating temperament?
vsm1.3:79.5: What suits one of what kind of temperament?
vsm1.3:80.1: Herein, as some say, the first three kinds of temperament to begin with have their source in previous habit;
vsm1.3:80.2: and they have their source in elements and humours.
vsm1.3:80.3: Apparently one of greedy temperament has formerly had plenty of desirable tasks and gratifying work to do,
vsm1.3:80.4: or has reappeared here after dying in a heaven.
vsm1.3:80.5: And one of hating temperament has formerly had plenty of stabbing and torturing and brutal work to do
vsm1.3:80.6: or has reappeared here after dying in one of the hells or the nāga (serpent) existences.
vsm1.3:80.7: And one of deluded temperament has formerly drunk a lot of intoxicants and neglected learning and questioning,
vsm1.3:80.8: or has reappeared here after dying in the animal existence.
vsm1.3:80.9: It is in this way that they have their source in previous habit, they say.
vsm1.3:81.1: Then a person is of deluded temperament because two elements are prominent,
vsm1.3:81.2: that is to say, the earth element and the water element.
vsm1.3:81.3: He is of hating temperament because the other two elements are prominent.
vsm1.3:81.4: But he is of greedy temperament because all four are equal.
vsm1.3:81.5: And as regards the humours, one of greedy temperament has phlegm in excess
vsm1.3:81.6: and one of deluded temperament has wind in excess.
vsm1.3:81.7: Or one of deluded temperament has phlegm in excess
vsm1.3:81.8: and one of greedy temperament has wind in excess.
vsm1.3:81.9: So they have their source in the elements and the humours, they say.
vsm1.3:82.1:
Now, it can rightly be objected that not all of those who have had plenty of desirable
tasks and gratifying work to do, and who have reappeared here after dying in a heaven,
vsm1.3:82.3: or the others respectively of hating and deluded temperament;
vsm1.3:82.4: and there is no such law of prominence of elements (see XIV.43f.) as that asserted;
vsm1.3:82.5: and only the pair, greed and delusion, are given in the law of humours, and even that subsequently contradicts itself;
vsm1.3:82.6: and no source for even one among those beginning with one of faithful temperament is given.
vsm1.3:83.1: The following is the exposition according to the opinion of the teachers of the commentaries;
vsm1.3:83.2: or this is said in the “explanation of prominence”:
vsm1.3:83.3:
“The fact that these beings have prominence of greed, prominence of hate,
prominence of delusion, is governed by previous root-cause.
vsm1.3:83.4: “For when in one man, at the moment of his accumulating rebirth-producing kamma, greed is strong and non-greed is weak,
vsm1.3:83.5: non-hate and non-delusion are strong and hate and delusion are weak,
vsm1.3:83.6: then his weak non-greed is unable to prevail over his greed,
vsm1.3:83.7: but his non-hate and non-delusion being strong are able to prevail over his hate and delusion.
vsm1.3:83.8: That is why, on being reborn through rebirth-linking given by that kamma,
vsm1.3:83.11: and possesses understanding with knowledge like a lightning flash.
vsm1.3:84.1: “When, at the moment of another’s accumulating kamma, greed and hate are strong and non-greed and non-hate weak,
vsm1.3:84.2: and non-delusion is strong and delusion weak,
vsm1.3:84.3: then in the way already stated he has both greed and hate
vsm1.3:84.4: but possesses understanding with knowledge like a lightning flash, like the Elder Datta-Abhaya.
vsm1.3:84.5: “When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, greed, non-hate and delusion are strong and the others are weak,
vsm1.3:84.6: then in the way already stated he both has greed and is dull
vsm1.3:84.7: but is good-tempered and unangry, like the Elder Bahula.
vsm1.3:84.8:
“Likewise when, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, the three, namely, greed,
hate and delusion are strong and non-greed, etc., are weak,
vsm1.3:84.9: then in the way already stated he has both greed and hate and is deluded.
vsm1.3:85.1: “When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed, hate and delusion are strong and the others are weak,
vsm1.3:85.2: then in the way already stated he has little defilement and is unshakable even on seeing a heavenly object,
vsm1.3:85.3: but he has hate and is slow in understanding.
vsm1.3:85.4: “When, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed, non-hate and non-delusion are strong and the rest weak,
vsm1.3:85.5: then in the way already stated he has no greed and no hate, and is good-tempered
vsm1.3:85.7: “Likewise when, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, non-greed, hate and non-delusion are strong and the rest weak,
vsm1.3:85.8: then in the way already stated he both has no greed and possesses understanding
vsm1.3:85.9: but has hate and is irascible.
vsm1.3:85.10:
“Likewise when, at the moment of his accumulating kamma, the three, that is, non-hate,
non-greed, and non-delusion, are strong and greed, etc., are weak,
vsm1.3:85.11: then in the way already stated he has no greed and no hate and possesses understanding, like the Elder Mahā-Saṅgharakkhita.”
vsm1.3:86.1: One who, as it is said here, “has greed” is one of greedy temperament;
vsm1.3:86.2: one who “has hate” and one who “is dull” are respectively of hating temperament and deluded temperament.
vsm1.3:86.3: One who “possesses understanding” is one of intelligent temperament.
vsm1.3:86.4: One who “has no greed” and one who “has no hate” are of faithful temperament because they are naturally trustful.
vsm1.3:86.5: Or just as one who is reborn through kamma accompanied by non-delusion is of intelligent temperament,
vsm1.3:86.6: so one who is reborn through kamma accompanied by strong faith is of faithful temperament,
vsm1.3:86.7: one who is reborn through kamma accompanied by thoughts of sense desire is of speculative temperament,
vsm1.3:86.8: and one who is reborn through kamma accompanied by mixed greed, etc., is of mixed temperament.
vsm1.3:86.9: So it is the kamma productive of rebirth-linking and accompanied by someone among the things beginning with greed
vsm1.3:86.10: that should be understood as the source of the temperaments.
vsm1.3:87.1: But it was asked, and how is it to be known that “This person is of greedy temperament?” (§79), and so on.
vsm1.3:87.3:
By the posture, by the action,
By eating, seeing, and so on,
By the kind of states occurring,
May temperament be recognized.
vsm1.3:88.2: when one of greedy temperament is walking in his usual manner, he walks carefully,
vsm1.3:88.4: puts it down evenly, lifts it up evenly,
vsm1.3:88.6: One of hating temperament walks as though he were digging with the points of his feet,
vsm1.3:88.7: puts his foot down quickly, lifts it up quickly,
vsm1.3:88.8: and his step is dragged along.
vsm1.3:88.9: One of deluded temperament walks with a perplexed gait,
vsm1.3:88.10: puts his foot down hesitantly, lifts it up hesitantly,
vsm1.3:88.11: and his step is pressed down suddenly.
vsm1.3:88.12: And this is said in the account of the origin of the Māgandiya Sutta:
vsm1.3:88.13: The step of one of greedy nature will be springy;
vsm1.3:88.14: The step of one of hating nature, dragged along;
vsm1.3:88.15: Deluded, he will suddenly press down his step;
vsm1.3:88.16: And one without defilement has a step like this.
vsm1.3:89.1: The stance of one of greedy temperament is confident and graceful.
vsm1.3:89.2: That of one of hating temperament is rigid.
vsm1.3:89.3: That of one of deluded temperament is muddled,
vsm1.3:89.5: And one of greedy temperament spreads his bed unhurriedly,
vsm1.3:89.6: lies down slowly, composing his limbs, and he sleeps in a confident manner.
vsm1.3:89.7: When woken, instead of getting up quickly,
vsm1.3:89.8: he gives his answer slowly as though doubtful.
vsm1.3:89.9: One of hating temperament spreads his bed hastily anyhow;
vsm1.3:89.10: with his body flung down he sleeps with a scowl.
vsm1.3:89.11: When woken, he gets up quickly and answers as though annoyed.
vsm1.3:89.12: One of deluded temperament spreads his bed all awry
vsm1.3:89.13: and sleeps mostly face downwards with his body sprawling.
vsm1.3:89.14: When woken, he gets up slowly, saying, “Hum.”
vsm1.3:90.1: Since those of faithful temperament, etc., are parallel to those of greedy temperament, etc.,
vsm1.3:90.2: their postures are therefore like those described above.
vsm1.3:90.3: This firstly is how the temperaments may be recognized by the posture.
vsm1.3:91.1: By the action: also in the acts of sweeping, etc.,
vsm1.3:91.2: one of greedy temperament grasps the broom well,
vsm1.3:91.3: and he sweeps cleanly and evenly without hurrying or scattering the sand, as if he were strewing sinduvāra flowers.
vsm1.3:91.4: One of hating temperament grasps the broom tightly,
vsm1.3:91.5: and he sweeps uncleanly and unevenly with a harsh noise, hurriedly throwing up the sand on each side.
vsm1.3:91.6: One of deluded temperament grasps the broom loosely,
vsm1.3:91.7: and he sweeps neither cleanly nor evenly, mixing the sand up and turning it over.
vsm1.3:92.1: As with sweeping, so too with any action such as washing and dyeing robes, and so on.
vsm1.3:92.2: One of greedy temperament acts skilfully, gently, evenly and carefully.
vsm1.3:92.3: One of hating temperament acts tensely, stiffly and unevenly.
vsm1.3:92.4: One of deluded temperament acts unskilfully as if muddled, unevenly and indecisively.
vsm1.3:92.5: Also one of greedy temperament wears his robe neither too tightly nor too loosely, confidently and level all round.
vsm1.3:92.6: One of hating temperament wears it too tight and not level all round.
vsm1.3:92.7: One of deluded temperament wears it loosely and in a muddled way.
vsm1.3:92.8: Those of faithful temperament, etc., should be understood in the same way as those just described, since they are parallel.
vsm1.3:92.9: This is how the temperaments may be recognized by the actions.
vsm1.3:93.1: By eating: One of greedy temperament likes eating rich sweet food.
vsm1.3:93.2: When eating, he makes a round lump not too big and eats unhurriedly, savouring the various tastes.
vsm1.3:93.4: One of hating temperament likes eating rough sour food.
vsm1.3:93.5: When eating he makes a lump that fills his mouth, and he eats hurriedly without savouring the taste.
vsm1.3:93.6: He is aggrieved when he gets something not good.
vsm1.3:93.7: One of deluded temperament has no settled choice.
vsm1.3:93.8: When eating, he makes a small un-rounded lump,
vsm1.3:93.9: and as he eats he drops bits into his dish, smearing his face, with his mind astray, thinking of this and that.
vsm1.3:93.10: Also those of faithful temperament, etc., should be understood in the same way as those just described since they are parallel.
vsm1.3:93.11: This is how the temperament may be recognized by eating.
vsm1.3:94.1: And by seeing and so on: when one of greedy temperament sees even a slightly pleasing visible object, he looks long as if surprised,
vsm1.3:94.4: and when departing, he does so with regret as if unwilling to leave.
vsm1.3:94.5: When one of hating temperament sees even a slightly unpleasing visible object, he avoids looking long as if he were tired,
vsm1.3:94.8: and when departing, he does so without regret as if anxious to leave.
vsm1.3:94.9: When one of deluded temperament sees any sort of visible object, he copies what others do:
vsm1.3:94.10: if he hears others criticizing, he criticizes;
vsm1.3:94.11: if he hears others praising, he praises;
vsm1.3:94.12: but actually he feels equanimity in himself—the equanimity of unknowing.
vsm1.3:94.13: So too with sounds, and so on.
vsm1.3:94.14: And those of faithful temperament, etc., should be understood in the same way as those just described since they are parallel.
vsm1.3:94.15: This is how the temperaments may be recognized by seeing and so on.
